one_line: A two-line text joke over a designer room, then the product as the punchline at 0:02, with no talking needed.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 static wide shot of a living room with leather armchairs, no person. Small white English text: "I used to have a living room". 0:02 cut to a foam cube and ramp on the rug: "now she does". No speech.
q1_hook.why: A joke every parent of a baby knows, in a text card on the first frame (K3, T3). The product arrives as the punchline at 0:02, after a cut every second or two (H1, E1). No person or voice in the first 3 s (H4, H6 not met), so it leans wholly on the text.

beats.what: Designer living room, armchairs then sofa; "I used to have a living room"
beats.why: Sets up the "before" in two quick shots

beats.what: A foam cube and ramp fill the rug; "now she does"
beats.why: The punchline lands at 2 s, product on screen

beats.what: A woman builds the set against a wooden wall, the pieces appearing fast
beats.why: Shows the set goes together quickly

beats.what: Close-ups of the leopard-print pouf, steps and tunnel; "baby entertainment but make it cute"
beats.why: States the value and shows the look

beats.what: A baby sits on the cube, then the pouf, the woman beside, no text
beats.why: A baby actually uses it, with an adult close

beats.what: Baby and woman at the cube; "ok she can keep the living room"
The set from the front; a child crawls through the tunnel, two others beside
beats.why: More children playing, a livelier last picture

beats.what: The woman pushes the ramp into place; "BLISS"

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None asked. The "living room" joke is a relatable moment a parent might send to another parent; the caption has no question, save or tag ask.
q2_flow.why: The joke opens a question at 0:00 and answers it at 0:19 (H5, K2). A new picture every 1 to 3 s keeps the pace (R3, E2). The 0:13 to 0:19 take repeats a few similar actions, and the ending is the brand word, not the payoff (R4).

q3_cta.what: None in the video or the caption. "BLISS" is the last text (0:23 to 0:24). The caption is "בקיצור זה הבית שלה" with emojis and the tag @bliss.il.
q3_cta.why: No next step: nothing says where to buy or what it costs (C6). The cost is small for a reach joke. The brand takes about 2 s of 25, the product shows many times, a benefit is named, and no engagement bait is used (C7, C2).

q4_shown.what: 0:02 a foam cube and ramp on a living-room rug. 0:04 to 0:08 a woman builds the set. 0:08 to 0:12 close-ups of the leopard-print pouf, steps and tunnel. 0:13 to 0:22 a baby on the pieces, then a child crawling through. No price.
q4_shown.why: The product arrives as the punchline at 0:02 and returns in several views, with the brand held to the last 2 s (S1, H3). The build shows it is simple, and a baby using it follows. Children's faces are on screen, which LumeBook's own Reels avoid (S5).

q5_edit.what: About 11 shots in 25 s, about 2.2 s each, straight cuts. The build looks time-compressed. Small white English text at 0:00, 0:02, 0:09, 0:19, 0:23. No speech. Ends mid-action on the woman pushing the ramp.
q5_edit.why: Five cuts in the first 9 s, then longer takes, a pace that suits a visual joke (E1, E2). The compressed build avoids dead time (R1). Text carries the whole message; audio could not be checked (E4). Ends right after the brand word, no tail (E8).

q6_topic.what: A parent joke ("I used to have a living room") selling a foam play set that looks good at home. Serves parents who want baby gear that fits their space.
q6_topic.why: A joke from a lived parenting moment, toys taking over the house, with a payoff line at 0:19 (K3, K1). A parent might send it to another parent (R5). The luxury home may feel far from most viewers; no principle in the list covers that.

q7_filmed.what: Static eye-level wide shots plus handheld close-ups of the pouf lid, steps and tunnel. Soft indoor light, a design-led home with wooden wall units. A woman seen from behind or in profile, a baby and two other children.
q7_filmed.why: The wide shots show the whole set at phone size and the close-ups show the material (F4). Steady, clean frames need no face (S4, F7). The designer interior and tripod-like frames give a polished look, less home-made than a typical creator Reel (H8).

q8_text.on_screen: Small thin white English text, centred at about 50% of the frame height, one or two lines: "I used to have a living room" (0:00), "now she does" (0:02), "baby entertainment but make it cute" (0:09), "ok she can keep the living room" (0:19), "BLISS" (0:23). No Hebrew on screen.
q8_text.caption: "בקיצור זה הבית שלה" followed by five emojis and the tag @bliss.il. A few Hebrew words, no hashtags, no question, no CTA, no disclosure words.
q8_text.why: Text is short and arrives with the picture, in the middle of the frame, inside the safe zone (T3, T4). But it is English only (T1), small and thin, white on cream and beige at times (T5). The caption has no product keywords or hashtags (T7), and no disclosure words beyond the tag (T8).

weak_points: No CTA, price or where to buy; English-only text for Hebrew viewers; a luxury home few share; thin white text on pale backgrounds; no disclosure words; babies' and children's faces on screen.
lumebook_takeaway: Copy the two-line text joke: a "before" shot, then the book arriving, hands only, tripod, Hebrew text, no child.
not_verified: Audio and music (the transcript is only "תודה רבה", which means no speech). Whether the woman is the account owner and the children are hers (her face is barely seen). Whether the build is sped up (frames are one per second; the set grows from one cube at 0:04 to all pieces at 0:07). Product names beyond "BLISS". Corrections to src/coded: the text "ok she can keep the living room" (0:19 to 0:21) is missing from the first pass; the woman is seen from behind or in profile, so "creator's face" is doubtful; about 11 shots, not 10.
